provenance: Authored public demonstration fixture with deliberate language errors and Unicode punctuation.
prompt: Some people think governments should spend more on public transport than on roads. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Government have to decide how to divide transport budgets between public services and roads. I believe that public transport should receive greater investment in cities, although maintaining safe roads remains necessary. A balanced policy can improve access to work while meeting the needs of people who cannot use a bus or train.

The main reason to prioritize public transport is affordability. Many worker can’t afford to own a car, especially when fuel, insurance and parking are considered together. Frequent buses gives these workers a practical way to reach more employers. For example, a bus route linking an outer suburb to a business district could allow residents to apply for jobs that were previously too far away. This  helps households and businesses at the same time.

Another benefit is that public transport can reduce traffic congestion. When a reliable train carries hundreds of passengers, some journeys that would otherwise be made by car can be avoided. However, new services will attract passengers only if they are frequent and convenient. Building a railway without useful connections may waste money, so investment should include bus links and simple ticketing.

Road spending still has an important role. Rural communities often depend on roads because their populations are too small to support frequent public services. Emergency vehicles and deliveries also need a safe road network. Governments should therefore repair damaged roads even when urban public transport receives the larger share of new investment.

In conclusion, I support prioritizing public transport in “densely populated” areas because it can improve affordability and reduce congestion. This policy should be combined with essential road maintenance and attention to rural access.
